sentences.text: On 18.02.023, some unknown persons threw a four pages letter in his house, wherein various allegations were made regarding working of Jawahar Edudation Society.

In the said letter, it is also mentioned that one Professor by name Mr. Prabhakar Karad, was in the habit of eating tobacco within the college premises and so also used to visit the college under influence of liquor.
It was also stated in the said letter that he had outraged the modesty of girls students and that some girls had allegedly undergone the abortions.
Various allegations of a serious nature were thus made against the said Professor Mr. Karad.
It is also stated in the said letter that some persons at the behest of the Member of Legislative Assembly were involved in preparation of forged document.
Allegations were also made regarding demand of money from three Professor belonging to Scheduled Caste category.
3. In short, the letter dated 18.02.2023 was not happily worded and was defamatory.

The applicants are alleged to have prepared a false and defamatory document by forging the signature of non applicant No.2 and seal,
stamp of the Society, and forwarded those documents to his Excellency the Governor, and various Government Officers and the institutions.

It is also 929 APPLN 1228.2023.odt 2 of 7  mentioned in the first information report that the applicants, namely, Sanjay Rankhambe, Somnath Kirwale, Sagar Shinde acting upon the directions of applicant Ramakant, have lodged a report against non applicant No.2 with Police Station and so also have filed proceeding in the Court.

4. It was further alleged in the first information report that the Ramakant Manikrao Phad And Others vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another on 27 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47010372/
2 complaints were also filed with the Chancellor of Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar University, Aurangabad in respect of which proceedings are pending.

sentences.text: Thus, it was suspected that the aforesaid letter dated 18.02.2023 was prepared by the present applicants.

5. In this background, learned Advocate for the applicants submitted that even if the contents of the first information report are taken to be true, no prima facie case is made out against the applicants.

He submitted that offences under Sections 420, 147, 468, 469, 501 read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code are wrongly registered against the present applicants though the ingredients of said offences are not satisfied.
He submitted that the FIR is based on merely suspicion and even a reading of FIR would show that the allegations are, at the most, defamatory in nature, which could be attributed to unknown persons.
Per contra, learned APP has contended that the investigation in the crime is under progress and during the course the same, the report of handwriting expert was sought.
He further submitted that the investigation papers reveal that specimen signature of the present applicants were obtained and forwarded for expert opinion.
Expert report though has not stated that the signatures on the letter were of the present applicants, but there is grave suspicion that applicants have committed the crime.
Therefore, he submits that the proceedings are not be entitled to be quashed.

7. Learned Advocate for non applicant No.2 has contended that since the first information report is registered, it is obligatory on the part of Ramakant Manikrao Phad And Others vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another on 27 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47010372/

8. With the help of respective learned Advocates, I have gone through the record of the case and have given thoughtful consideration to the arguments advanced.

9. The Hon'ble Apex Court in case of State of Haryana and others Vs. Bhajan Lal and others, 1992 Suppl (1) SCC 335 had laid down principles 929 APPLN 1228.2023.odt 4 of 7  for the quashment of the first information report.

entities.text: State of Haryana and others Vs. Bhajan Lal and others, 1992 Suppl (1) SCC 335
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: One of the tests is whether the man of ordinary prudence would arrive at a conclusion, after reading the contents of FIR/final report, that offence is made out or not.
The second test for the quashing of first information report is whether the first information discloses prima facie case and ingredients of the offence.
One of the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court is whether the proceedings are initiated with mala fide intention or not.
The criteria for quashment of FIR also includes whether the investigation can be allowed to be carried out if the non cognizable offence is disclosed and the permission of Magistrate is not obtained.
10. It is in the light of the aforesaid parameters that the contents of the first information report are required to be taken into consideration.

11. Admittedly, it is the case of the prosecution so also non applicant No.2 that on 18.02.2023, a four pages letter was dropped/thrown in his Ramakant Manikrao Phad And Others vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another on 27 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47010372/
4 house, which was containing the defamatory statements.

entities.text: Ramakant Manikrao Phad And Others vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said statements were made against one Professor Mr. Karad and further it speaks about the alleged illegalities going on in the Jawahar Education Society.
The contents of the letter also speaks about alleged involvement of the Member of Legislative Assembly in the affairs of the said society.
Be that as it may, at the most, a perusal of the first information report would reveal that a letter containing false or defamatory statements was dropped at the house of non applicant No.2.

There is absolutely no material on record to show that the present applicants were in any manner connected with the preparation of the aforesaid letter or with forging the signature of non applicant No.2.
Suspicion, however strong, cannot take place of the proof.
13. Learned APP Mr. Badakh has submitted that the statement of postman has been recorded, who states that he has delivered the aforesaid letter to the addresses.
However, mere delivery of this letter at the instance of postman would not be enough to connect the present applicants to the crime involved.

14. I could not see anything in the first information report that there was any fraudulent intention at initial stage to cheat the non applicant No.2 and therefore Section 420 of IPC could not have been registered against the applicants.
So far as the forgery is concerned, nothing has been brought on the record that the present applicants have committed the said forgery.

As far as the offence of defamation is concerned, it is necessary to mention here that the same is non cognizable and non applicant No.2, if desires, can always take Ramakant Manikrao Phad And Others vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another on 27 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47010372/

15. In that view of matter, continuation of criminal prosecution would be an abuse of process of law and therefore, following order is passed.
ORDER (i) Criminal Application is allowed.

(ii) FIR No. 44/2023, dated 22.02.2023, registered with Parali City Police Station, District Beed for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 417, 468, 469, 501 read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code is quashed and set aside.
